\begin{example} \end{example}[Cellular homology of closed nonorientable surfaces] ↗ thm:cellular-singular-homology-isomorphic 1. ch2:2.37\group Cellular Homology

For the nonorientable genus-$g$ surface with attaching word $a_1^2\cdots a_g^2$, $d_2(1)=(2,\ldots ,2)$ and $d_1=0$. Hence $H_2=0$ and $H_1\cong \mathbb {Z}^{g-1}\oplus \mathbb {Z}_2$. \end{example}
